h1: The 8 Best Induction Cooktops Under $500, From Countertop Doubles to Built-In Ranges, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 induction cooktops under $500, portable doubles and 240V built-ins, scored on burners, power, control range and safety.
summary: The Nuwave Double Pro is the best induction cooktop under $500 for most kitchens, with two burners and a 50 to 575 degree F range from a plug-in countertop unit. The VEVOR 30-inch built-in is the pick if you want five burners and will hardwire it, the Duxtop 9620LS is the simple LCD double, and the Nuwave Induction Wok is the specialist for stir-fry.
intro: The first decision in this price range is not which model but which kind: a countertop unit you plug into a wall, or a built-in cooktop that needs a 240V circuit and a cutout in your counter. Both sit under $500, and they could not be less alike. Buying a built-in for a rental flat, or a countertop double for a family of six, are the two ways people end up returning an induction cooktop.

Eight cooktops are ranked here, split between portable doubles, a wok unit and 240V built-ins. Scoring weighs burner count, rated power, control range, safety features and how much installation each demands. Every figure comes from a listing, and where a spec is missing we say so.

products.name: Nuwave Double Pro Cooktop Induction Countertop Burner
products.verdict: Two burners with a wide 50 to 575 degree F range, on a plug-in countertop unit.
products.description:
The Double Pro is a portable dual-burner induction cooktop with a temperature range of 50 to 575 degrees F. It sits on a counter and plugs into a standard outlet, so there is no wiring.

It takes first place because it combines two burners with fine temperature control, and that is the useful combination in a home kitchen. A low end of 50 degrees F lets you hold sauces warm or melt chocolate without scorching, and 575 degrees F is hot enough for searing. Two burners let you run a pan and a pot together. The catch with any plug-in double is that both burners share one circuit, so running both at full power will draw down output on each.

Buy it if you want flexible cooking without installation. Skip it if you regularly cook for large groups at once.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that want precise heat control.
products.skipIf: You cook for large groups with four pots.

products.name: VEVOR Built-in Induction Electric Stove Top 30-Inch
products.verdict: A 30-inch built-in with five burners, nine power levels, sensor touch and a child lock.
products.description:
The VEVOR 30-inch is a 240V built-in cooktop with 5 burners, 9 power levels, sensor touch controls and a child safety lock. It is designed to be dropped into a counter cutout, not to sit on top.

It ranks second because five burners in a standard 30-inch footprint is the most cooking surface per dollar in this ranking. The child lock is a real feature in a family kitchen, since touch controls can be triggered by a stray hand or a cat. The requirements are the cost: a 240V circuit, a hardwire connection by someone qualified and a countertop cutout that matches.

Buy it if you are replacing a cooktop and have the right circuit. Skip it if you rent or cannot wire a 240V line.
products.idealFor: Kitchen upgrades with a 240V circuit available.

products.name: Duxtop 9620LS Portable Double Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: A straightforward 1800W two-burner countertop cooktop with an LCD display.
products.description:
The Duxtop 9620LS is a portable two-burner induction cooktop with 1800W of total power and an LCD display. It is a countertop unit, simple to set up and use.

The 1800W figure is the number to understand: it is shared across both burners, so a single pan can use close to the full amount, while two pans split it. That makes it ideal for one big job and one small one, but slow if you try to boil two large pots. It sits behind the Nuwave because the listing offers no temperature range, so you work from power levels instead of degrees.

Buy it if you want a no-fuss double that is easy to store. Skip it if you need exact temperature numbers.
pros: Two burners on a plug-in unit
products.idealFor: Dorms, RVs and apartments needing extra burners.

products.name: AMZCHEF 30-Inch Built-In Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: A hardwired 30-inch cooktop with a 10,600W rating and nine power levels.
products.description:
The AMZCHEF 30-inch is a 240V built-in cooktop with nine power levels and a 10,600W total rating. It has no plug and must be hardwired.

A 10,600W rating is the highest in this ranking, though it is a combined figure across all burners that cannot be reached by one pan alone. It sits fourth because the listing gives little about burner count or controls, and hardwiring is a job for a licensed electrician. If you are already replacing a gas or radiant cooktop with a 240V line in place, it is competitive.

Buy it if you have a 240V circuit ready and want a high-output unit. Skip it if you want to see burner details first.
cons: Burner details not in the listing
products.idealFor: Replacing a cooktop where 240V already exists.

products.name: Nuwave Induction Wok
products.verdict: A wok-shaped induction burner with 600, 900 and 1500W settings and 5 degree control steps.
products.description:
The Nuwave Induction Wok is built for round-bottomed woks, with three wattage settings of 600, 900 and 1500W, and a range from 100 to 575 degrees F in 5 degree steps.

A flat induction burner heats only where the pan touches, which is why woks work poorly on them. A curved surface keeps the wok in contact on the sides, so tossing and searing behave more like a flame. It ranks fifth because it is a one-job device: great for stir-fry, awkward for a flat pan or a stockpot.

Buy it if you cook a lot of wok dishes. Skip it if you want one general-purpose burner.
products.idealFor: Stir-fry cooks who want induction control.

products.name: Duxtop 9720LCBI Portable Induction Cooktop 2 Burner
products.verdict: A near-twin of the 9620LS with 1800W total, two burners and an LCD display.
products.description:
The Duxtop 9720LCBI is another portable double burner with 1800W total, an LCD display and two cooking zones. It reads like the 9620LS on paper, and the listing gives no distinguishing detail.

That sameness is why it ranks sixth: with no extra feature to point to, the choice between the two Duxtops is a coin toss. It still offers the same strengths of a plug-in design and a clear display.

Buy it if it is the better price on the day. Skip it if you want a temperature-based unit like the Nuwave.
products.idealFor: Anyone choosing between Duxtop doubles on price.

products.name: VEVOR Electric Cooktop 5 Burners 36-Inch Built-In
products.verdict: A 36-inch, five-burner built-in with 9,200W, nine heating levels and a child lock.
products.description:
The 36-inch VEVOR offers 5 burners, 9,200W, 9 heating levels, an LED touch screen and a child lock. It is a built-in unit for a 36-inch cutout.

It ranks seventh because a 36-inch cutout is far less common than a 30-inch one, so most buyers would have to modify the counter. In return you get extra room between burners. The listing calls it an electric cooktop, so confirm that the surface is induction before buying and that the cookware you own is magnetic.

Buy it if you already have a 36-inch opening. Skip it if you have a 30-inch cutout.

products.name: Nuwave PIC Double Pro Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: A dual-burner Nuwave with IMD touch controls, in a portable countertop design.
products.description:
The PIC Double Pro is a dual-burner countertop cooktop with IMD touch controls. The listing gives no wattage or temperature range.

It ranks last because it is a close relative of the Double Pro with less documentation, so there is no reason to prefer it. IMD touch controls are smooth, easy to wipe clean and give no crevices for grease.

Buy it if you find it priced below the first-place Double Pro. Skip it if you want published temperature figures.
pros: Two burners on a plug-in unit
cons: Little to prefer over the Double Pro
products.idealFor: A Nuwave double at a lower price.

whatMatters.detail: A double portable unit rated 1800W gives that total to both burners. One pan can use most of it, two pans split it. If you boil two large pots together, expect slow results.
A built-in cooktop needs a 240V circuit, a countertop cutout and usually an electrician. A portable unit plugs into any 120V outlet. Choose based on your kitchen and whether you rent.

A range from 50 to 575 degrees F, as on the Nuwave Double Pro, supports both warming and searing. Units listing only power levels give less control for sous-vide-style or candy work. Check for degree figures on the listing.

Induction heats only magnetic cookware, such as cast iron and many stainless pans. A fridge magnet that sticks to the base is the quick test. Aluminium and copper pans without a magnetic layer will not heat.
A child lock stops touch controls from changing settings by accident. Both VEVOR built-ins include one. For portable units, an auto-shutoff and a cool-to-touch surface matter in a busy kitchen.

faq.q: Will my pans work on induction?
faq.a: Only magnetic ones. Cast iron and many stainless steel pans work, while pure aluminium and copper do not. Hold a magnet to the base: if it sticks firmly, the pan will heat.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying an induction cooktop?
faq.a: Skipping the electrical check. Built-in units need 240V and a hardwired connection, and a double portable unit needs a dedicated outlet. Confirm before ordering.

faq.q: Is a built-in worth it over a portable double?
faq.a: If you are replacing a cooktop, yes, for the extra burners and tidy look. If you rent or want flexibility, a portable double like the Nuwave is a better fit.
Some produce a faint buzz at certain power levels, especially with thin pans. It is usually a pan issue rather than a defect. Heavier pans are quieter.

faq.q: How do I clean the glass?
faq.a: Wipe with a damp cloth once it has cooled and use a ceramic cooktop cleaner for burnt-on spills. Avoid abrasive pads that scratch the glass.

faq.q: Can I use a portable unit as my main cooktop?
faq.a: For one or two people, yes, and many do. Larger families will want the burner count of a built-in. Check the shared wattage on doubles.

finalTake: For most kitchens, the Nuwave Double Pro is the best induction cooktop under $500, with two burners, a 50 to 575 degree F range and no installation. If you can hardwire 240V, the VEVOR 30-inch gives five burners and a child lock for similar money. The Duxtop 9620LS is the simple double, and the Nuwave Induction Wok is the specialist. Check the circuit and your pans before you click buy.
